title: Homeroom Android app never gets past the splash screen
where: Whole screen, every route (17 of 17 on each shape)
why: Every Android app capture, on both the small phone and the sideways tablet, is the same cream screen with the Homeroom wordmark: the frames are byte-identical across home, messages, hub, request and settings. Nothing in the shell ever drew, so on these shapes no screen can be reviewed and a real user would be stuck on the splash. This may be the harness's Android bridge rather than the product, but as captured it is a total failure and should be confirmed first. No Android-convention review (back arrow, overflow menu, status/nav bar insets) was possible.

title: Landscape: the side rail draws on top of the page header
where: Top-left, the header row over the rail (y about 120-180 pt)
why: On Communities, Homeroom bot, Messages, DM, group, the App tabs and the request page, the rail's first row (house icon and 'Home') sits on top of the header's sidebar toggle and page title. You get 'Home' overprinted on 'Communities' / 'Messages' / 'Homeroom bot', and on the hub-open shot the title 'Neighbourhood Swap' runs half-faded under the rail and half-bold beside it. On the request page a pale green band covers the rail's top. It looks broken and covers both the sidebar toggle and the page title. Home, Discover, Profile, Settings and the hub do not overlap, so this is position or stacking on some screens only.

title: Landscape Homeroom bot: list column too narrow, heading spills out of its card
where: Middle column (list card) between the rail and the chat
why: The list column is about 170 pt wide. 'Homeroom bot' wraps onto two lines and 'Homeroom' is cut off at the card's right edge. 'Needs you: 1 · In progress: 0' breaks one word per line down the card. The project chip shows only 'Book C' and the Main Chat row is pushed below the fold. The rail, list and chat each get a third of 852 pt, and the list's third cannot hold its own header.

title: Landscape Discover: app names broken mid-word and cut off
where: ALL APPS grid, the two cards in the first row
why: Each card fits an icon, the title and a filled Join pill into about 220 pt. The titles come out as 'Grou / p...' and 'Sign- / up...', and the subtitle as 'Upda...'. You cannot tell what the apps are, and the Join button is the widest thing on the card. Use one column here, or put Join under the title.

title: Request page with the keyboard up leaves no room for the thread
where: Request card between the title and the Reply box
why: When Reply is focused, the request card shrinks to its title. The thread is one sliced line: '(#1) · 9:15 PM' cut through the glyphs on iPhone, and a half-avatar plus clipped name on Android. In landscape only the Workshop pill and the Reply box remain. On Android and in landscape the jump-to-latest chevron also covers the title ('vote on the n[v]one'). You cannot see what you are replying to, and the large title block stays on screen while the content goes.

title: Landscape chats with the keyboard up show only the composer
where: Chat pane, right of the rail
why: In a sideways DM or group, focusing the message box removes the conversation header and every message. Only the outlined composer is left at the top of an empty card. The Homeroom bot chat keeps only the clipped bottom of the last card. Meanwhile the 270 pt rail and the full app header stay visible, so the space goes to navigation instead of the conversation you are typing into.

title: Floating chat buttons sit on top of the messages
where: Top-right of the message list, the members and ••• discs
why: The members and ••• buttons float over the scrolling thread with no backing bar. In the Android group they cover the '@audit_ada 9:14 PM' sender line. On iPhone they sit on the first visible bubble. In the DM with the keyboard up, ••• sits on 'has the numbers'. Text shows through around them, and a tap meant for the bubble lands on the menu.

title: Jump-to-latest chevron covers message text
where: Centre of the request thread, just above the Reply box
why: The round down-chevron is placed over body text: 'top with the[v]tup date' on Android, and over the bold 'Let members su[v]gest a book' in landscape. It hides words in the one message on screen. Pin it beside the composer or into the gutter, not over content.

title: Request card: 'See progress' button sliced off under the title
where: Request card, just under 'Let members suggest a book and vote on the next one'
why: The thread scrolls under the sticky title block. The blue 'See progress' button and its white card are cut through the middle by a hard edge with no fade or divider. It reads as a rendering glitch, not as scrolled content.

title: Workshop and proposals links open the Hub instead
where: Whole project page
why: The captures for the project's Workshop and its proposals list both show the Book Club hub: the header says 'Hub' on phones, and 'Hub' is the lit rail row in landscape. The two are identical to the plain hub. A link to the Workshop or to proposals lands somewhere else, and on a phone no Hub/Workshop switch is visible to recover.

title: Project name breaks mid-word on Home's My apps tiles
where: My apps row, label under the N tile
why: 'Neighbourhood Swap' wraps as 'Neighbourh / ood Swap' on iPhone, 'Neighbour / hood Swap' on Android and 'Neighbourhoo / d Swap' in landscape. The label is force-broken inside a word instead of truncating or wrapping at the space. On 360 px 'New project' also wraps to two lines, so the labels in the row have uneven heights.

title: Group chat listed under 'Direct messages'
where: Messages list section label; landscape rail under Messages
why: 'Flat 4B' is a 3-member group ('you own this group'), but it is the first row under the DIRECT MESSAGES label on the phone list. The landscape rail also files it under 'Direct messages'. That label is wrong as soon as anyone has a group.

title: Messages list looks different on a phone held upright and held sideways
where: Conversation rows
why: Upright, the rows are bare on the background: no card, no time, a single avatar, and regular-weight titles that do not match the 15/650 row title. Sideways, the same rows sit in a 20 px card with bold titles, '16m ago', a stacked group avatar and a members chip. Upright, the screen also has a large empty area under two rows. It is one component with two designs, and the upright one breaks house style.

title: Bottom tab bar: Communities tab misaligned, labels crowd at 360 px
where: Bottom tab bar
why: Only Communities draws its icon inside a rounded tile (a 'B' tile on a project page). Its label sits about 3 pt lower than the other four, and its lit pill is taller than the Home/Messages/You pills. At 360 px the labels almost touch: 'Communities' runs into the gap before 'Homeroom bot', and the lit Homeroom bot pill butts against 'Messages'. The bar looks uneven, and the targets have almost no space between them.

title: Landscape rail takes a third of the width and squeezes every page
where: Left rail, about 270 of 852 pt
why: On a phone held sideways the full-width rail stays open by default. Settings then has three columns, so the list truncates 'Linked ph...'. The Communities row subtitle cuts off at '1 in progress · 2 new messages · 3 ...'. The hub subtitle wraps 'Private community · 3 / members' beside its buttons. Home shows only four app tiles above the fold. A collapsed icon rail would give the content the room it needs.

title: Hub says nothing to vote on while a vote is waiting
where: Hub 'For you' card, first line
why: In the same Android run the request shows an 'Up for a vote' pill, and the hub captured after it still says 'Nothing more to vote on.'. Communities in landscape says '1 vote waiting on you · Book Club' with Review. The hub is the page that should send you to the vote. The wording 'Nothing more' is also odd when nothing was voted on.

title: Request thread: internal wording and repeated content
where: Request thread body
why: The activity line reads 'audit_ada created issue: "Let members suggest..." (#1)'. 'Issue' is the internal word; the page calls it a REQUEST. That line also has a stray bullet with a deep indent, and it sits below a 'No replies yet' divider. On Android and in landscape the first message repeats the card title word for word as a bold heading, so the same sentence fills the top of a short screen twice.

title: Request page: two back buttons, and the header says 'Hub'
where: Header back disc, plus the '‹ Workshop' pill below it
why: The header has a back chevron and its subtitle reads 'Book Club / Hub'. Directly under it is a second back control, '‹ Workshop'. Two stacked back buttons, and a header naming a tab you are not on, leave it unclear which one goes where.

title: Hub 'For you' card nearly touches the screen edges
where: FOR YOU card on the hub
why: The card is inset about 5 pt from each side. The hero above it, the FOR YOU label, and the cards on Communities, Profile and Settings use about 16 pt. The card looks wider than everything else on the page.

title: Hub Discussion row truncates its time to '· 9...'
where: Discussion #general row in the For you card
why: The preview '@audit_ben: Works for me 📚 · 9...' loses the timestamp to an ellipsis because the '2 new' pill and the chevron take the right side. A bare '9...' means nothing. Drop the time, or truncate the message text instead of the time.

title: Project name shown as a large heading more than once
where: Hub header and hero
why: On phones 'Book Club' is both the header title and the large hero name, directly under each other. In landscape the page has two large headings, 'Hub' and 'Book Club', plus 'Book Club' in the header. House style allows one large heading per page.

title: Project header changes colour between the project's own tabs
where: Top header bar on a project
why: On the Hub and the request page the header is solid project-green with white text and a white bell. On the same project's App tab it is the light shell header with a close X. Moving between tabs of one project flips the whole chrome, so it reads as leaving the project.

title: Homeroom bot list: repeated title and counts written as 'label: n'
where: Bot card header and the In progress section
why: The page header says 'Homeroom bot' and the card under it repeats it as a large heading. The subtitle says 'In progress: 1', and the section below repeats 'IN PROGRESS · 1'. House style asks for counts as phrases ('1 in progress') said once. The in-progress row truncates its own title to 'Let members suggest a b...' while the 'Homeroom bot' attribution takes a third of the row. The Watering Rota chip is also cut at the card edge.

title: Audience names differ between filters and the hub
where: Communities filter chips; hub subtitle
why: The chips say 'Public 2 / Private 1 / Just you 1', and the hub calls Book Club a 'Private community'. Elsewhere the product names audiences Group / Community / Just you. Book Club is a Group, so 'Private community' and 'Private' are a third set of words for the same idea.

title: Settings: odd search field, crowded rows, repeated labels
where: Settings list
why: 'Find a setting' is a grey, bordered rectangle that looks disabled. Every other search (Discover, Communities, Messages) is a white pill. A large empty gap follows it before ACCOUNT. Each row carries both a chevron and a bookmark, which truncates subtitles ('GitHub and X, for your wee...', 'Phones signed in with the ...'). The section ACCOUNT opens with a row called Account, and 'AI MODELS & USAGE' holds 'AI usage & models'.

title: Landscape Settings: Edit profile chevron sits outside its card
where: Right detail pane, Profile > Edit profile
why: The white Edit profile card ends before its chevron, so the '>' floats on the background to the right of the card. The pane also shows two large headings, 'Profile' and 'Sign-in'.

title: Profile shows zero counts as big stat tiles
where: Two tiles under the profile card
why: '0 live' and '0 challenges' fill two full-width tiles. House style says a zero shows nothing. A new member's profile opens on two large zeros.

title: Challenges page: repeated title, bare empty state
where: Leaderboard / Challenges screen
why: The header says 'Challenges' and the selected segment repeats 'Challenges'. Under it is one grey line, 'No challenges right now.', then a blank page with no next step and no explanation of Standings.

title: Discover: 'For you' shows a list titled ALL APPS
where: Discover, first card
why: With 'For you' selected the card is labelled ALL APPS, though Home sends you here from 'Discover Communities'. The rows are very tall: a large gap separates the title from 'Updated 22m ago', and each row has a 44 pt filled Join pill. Only two or three items fit on a phone.

title: Home section headings use mixed capitalisation
where: Home section headings
why: 'My apps' and 'Challenges' are sentence case, but 'Discover Communities' capitalises the second word. All three are large headings on one page, where house style allows one.

title: Header title and subtitle truncate on a 360 px phone
where: Top header
why: The App tab header cuts 'Neighbourhood Swap' to 'Neighbourhood S...', and the group header subtitle to '3 members · you own this gr...'. The bell and the account chip with its chevron take the space. A two-word project name should fit.

title: The same person is drawn differently from screen to screen
where: Sender names and avatars
why: In the DM the sender is 'audit_ben'; in the group the same person is '@audit_ben'. audit_ada's avatar is blue in the hub's 'active this week' row, purple on the request page and pale blue on Profile. Inconsistent name format and colour make one person look like several.

title: Landscape rail: grey dot on 'App' and a bare number badge
where: Rail rows under a project, and the Book Club row
why: The lit 'App' row has an unexplained grey status dot on the right, though house style keeps a dot for something wrong. Book Club carries a blue '1' disc with no words, where house style asks for a phrase ('1 to vote').

title: Android Chrome gets iPhone-style controls
where: Back buttons and overflow menus
why: On Android the header back is an iOS chevron in a disc rather than an arrow, and every overflow menu is a horizontal ••• rather than Android's vertical ⋮. These look foreign to Android users. If the Homeroom Android app renders the same shell, it will have the same problem; that could not be checked because the app captures stayed on the splash.
